translations.text: Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in the region of Philippi, together with the bishops and deacons.
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God whenever I remember you,
always offering prayers with joy in every petition of mine for all of you,
because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now.
I am confident of this: the one who began the good work in you will complete it by the day of Jesus Christ.
It is indeed right for me to think this about all of you, because I hold you in my heart, and both in my imprisonment and in my defense and confirmation of the gospel, you all share in grace with me.
God is my witness how I long for all of you with the compassion of Christ Jesus.
And this is what I pray: that your love may abound more and more in knowledge and all understanding,
so that you may choose what is best and be steadfast and without stumbling on the day of Christ,
filled with the fruits of righteousness through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
I want you to know, brothers, that what happened to me has served all the more to advance the gospel,
so that my imprisonment for Christ has become known throughout the whole court and to everyone else,
and many brothers in the Lord, encouraged by my imprisonment, have become even bolder in speaking the word of God without fear.
Some preach Christ out of envy and rivalry, and others out of goodwill.
Some do so out of love, because they know that I am here to defend the gospel.
Others proclaim Christ out of contentiousness, not sincerely, thinking that they will add affliction to my imprisonment.
But what does it matter? In whatever way, whether as a pretense or in truth, Christ is proclaimed, and in this I rejoice. Indeed, I will continue to rejoice,
For I know that this will lead to my salvation through your prayers and the gifts of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.

in keeping with my eager expectation and hope that I will not be put to shame in anything, but that with complete boldness, as always, so now also Christ will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.
For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
But if I live in the flesh, this means fruitful work for me, and I do not know what I will choose.
I am torn between the two: I desire to depart and be with Christ, which I consider far better,
but to remain here in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
Confident of this, I know that I will stay and remain with all of you for your growth and joy in faith,
so that through my coming to you again, your boasting in Christ Jesus may abound because of me.

Only conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel, so that whether I come and see you or remain far away and hear about you, you stand firm in one spirit and strive together with one soul for the faith of the gospel.
And do not be frightened in any way by your opponents. This is a sign of their destruction and of your salvation.
And this is from God: you have been granted, for Christ’s sake, not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him.
Having the same struggle that you saw in me and now hear about from me.
So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any fellowship in the Spirit, any compassion and mercy,
Make my joy complete: think alike, have the same love within you, and be united in spirit and purpose.
do nothing out of rivalry or empty conceit, but in humility consider one another better than yourselves.
Let each person look not only to their own interests, but also to those of their neighbor.
Let each of you have the same mindset that was also in Christ Jesus,
who was in the form of God and did not consider being equal to God an act of robbery,
but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, becoming like human beings and being found in appearance as a man.
He humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.
Therefore God also exalted him above all and granted him the name that is above every name,
so that at the name of Jesus Christ every knee should bow, of those in heaven, on earth, and in the underworld,
and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have obeyed in everything, not only when I was present but even more now that I am far from you, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
For it is God who enables you both to will and to act for his good pleasure.
Do everything without grumbling or muttering,
so that you may be blameless and pure, innocent children of God amid a stubborn and crooked generation, among whom you shine as lights in the world,
holding the word of life within yourselves, so that I may boast on the day of Christ that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
But even if I am offered up upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and share in the joy of all of you.
Likewise, you too should rejoice and share in my joy.
But I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that my heart too may be comforted when I learn how you are.
For I have no one else of the same mind who would genuinely care for you.
For everyone seeks their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
But you too know his proven character, for he served with me in the gospel as a son serves with his father.
So I hope to send him as soon as I am certain about my own situation.
But I trust in the Lord that I myself will also come soon.
But I considered it good to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, your messenger and the one who attends to my needs.
For he himself greatly longs to see all of you and was distressed because you had heard that he was ill.
Indeed, he was sick and near death, but God had mercy on him, and not on him alone but also on me, so that I would not suffer sorrow upon sorrow.
So I sent him promptly, so that you may rejoice when you see him again, and I may be free from sorrow.
Receive him in the Lord with all joy, and hold people like him in honor.
For he came near death for the Lord's work, laboring at the risk of his life to make up for what was lacking in your service to me.
Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. Writing the same things to you is no trouble for me, and it is a strong safeguard for you.
Beware of the dogs; beware of the evil workers; beware of the mutilation.
For we are the circumcision, we who worship by the Spirit of God and boast in Christ Jesus, and do not place our confidence in the flesh.
Yet I myself also have grounds for confidence in the flesh. If anyone else thinks he can have confidence in the flesh, I have even more:
circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrew descent; as to the law, a Pharisee;
as to zeal, I persecuted the church; as to righteousness under the law, I was blameless.
But whatever was gain to me, I consider loss for Christ's sake.
Indeed, I also consider everything a loss because of the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ our Lord. For his sake I was deprived of everything, and I consider it dung, so that I may gain Christ
and be found in him, not having any righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but the righteousness through faith in Christ, which is the righteousness from God through faith,
to know him and the power of his resurrection and the sharing in his sufferings, becoming like him in his death,
so that somehow I may attain the resurrection from the dead.
Not that I have already obtained it or have already been made perfect, but I pursue it so that I may take hold of it, since Christ Jesus has indeed taken hold of me.
Brothers, I do not consider myself to have attained it. But there is one thing: I forget what lies behind and reach forward to what lies ahead.
With my attention fixed, I run toward the goal of God's calling in Christ Jesus.
Therefore, all of you who are mature, think this way. And if you think differently about anything, God will reveal that to you as well.
But let us think in accordance with what we have attained and be united in following the same rule.
Become imitators of me, brothers, and take note of those who walk in this way, just as you have us as an example.
For many walk as enemies of the cross of Christ. I have often spoken to you about them, and now I speak even with tears.
Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is their shame. They think only of earthly things.
But our way of life is in heaven, from where we also await the Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
who will renew our lowly body to make it like his glorious body, by the power through which he is able to subject everything to himself.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, whom I long for, my joy and crown, stand firm in the Lord in this way, beloved.
I urge Euodia and I urge Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord.

Yes, I also ask you, my trusted companion and fellow worker, to help those who struggled alongside me in the gospel, together with Clement and my other fellow workers, whose names are in the book of life.
Rejoice in the Lord at all times. Again I say, rejoice!
Let your gentleness be known to everyone. The Lord is near.
Do not worry about anything, but in everything let your requests be made known to God through prayer and petition, with thanksgiving.
And the peace of God, which is beyond all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is loving, whatever has a good reputation, whatever is virtuous, whatever is praiseworthy—think about these things.
Do what you learned and received and heard and saw in me, and the God of peace will be with you.
I rejoiced greatly in the Lord because you too have thought of caring for me. Indeed, you were already concerned, but you were [?] concerning me.
I am not saying this because of any need, for I have learned to make do with what I can.
I know how to have little, and I know how to have plenty. In everything and in every way I have learned both to be full and to be hungry, both to have plenty and to have little.
I can do all things through the one who strengthened me.
Nevertheless, you did well to share in my distress.
You Philippians also know that at the beginning of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone.
For even in Thessalonica you sent supplies for my needs both once and a second time.
It is not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that increases to your account.
But I have received everything and have more than enough. I have received what came from you through Epaphroditus and am fully supplied—a sweet fragrance, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
And may my God meet all your needs according to his abundance in glory in Christ Jesus.
Now to our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus.
The brothers who are with me greet you.
All the saints greet you, especially those of Caesar’s household.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. The letter to the Philippians was written from Rome through Epaphroditus.
